chapter: Chicago cafes and the Browns band
title: Joe Frisco and show people raving about the band at a party
summary: Show-business figures including Joe Frisco and Sophie Tucker loved the band at a party; Frisco's natural stutter and his appreciation of jazz bands for his dance act.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And little Lester Allen, that comedian that was with White Scandals, he was there. All kinds of big people in show business. They were all at that party that night. I can't remember all of them.
Because theater treasures had a close contact with them.

That's right. The legit theaters. They were all there, and Joe Frisco went nuts about our band. He didn't even dance. All he did all night long from the time we started to play, he just sat on a chair right in front of the bandstand and went out of his noodle about this band. A lot of the others did too, Sophie Tucker, all of them. They thought they were really paying attention to that band.
Joe Frisco, it was always a real stutter with him, wasn't it?
Yeah, that was never put on. That was perfectly natural and normal.
Well, I told you, if we jazz enthusiasts wanted to look for a patron saint, it would be Joe Frisco,
I said. That's right. Yeah. You're not missing the mark much there, I'll tell you that.
He was certainly an early man to appreciate what a jazz band could do for an act.
Because for his dance, he needed a great band.
